messages:
support: FYI PulseAI reported a big throughput drop on their Dedicated pool this morning, started ~08:10 UTC. Requests are timing out or getting very low qps compared to baseline.

alex: seeing this in the alerting graph now, 80% drop in throughput on pool d-pulse-01, latency up from 45ms -> 220ms.

maria: any recent config changes to scheduler or batching params in that pool?

sam: we rolled the scheduler patch last night (token-slicing fairness heuristic). Could be related.

alex: repro notes from support:
- sends steady stream of 100 concurrent short requests (avg 12 tokens).
- observed many tiny microbatches of 1-2 tokens forming instead of being coalesced.
- gpu util low (20-30%) while token latency high.

kai: that sounds like continuous-batcher starving for fillers -> frequent kernel launches, poor throughput. Could be max_batch_tokens or prefill window misaligned.

infra-bot: [deploybot] rolled scheduler v2.3.7 to d-pool-02 at 2026-03-15T23:45:10Z by sam.

alex: attaching short log snippet from the serving runtime:
```
2026-03-16T08:09:58Z INFO batcher: new microbatch size=2 tokens=24 wait_ms=12
2026-03-16T08:09:58Z INFO batcher: dispatch to gpu run_id=abcd token_total=24
2026-03-16T08:09:59Z WARN scheduler: prefill-miss tenant=pulse tenant_q=0.03
2026-03-16T08:10:01Z INFO batcher: new microbatch size=1 tokens=10 wait_ms=118
```

maria: wait_ms 118 on single-token microbatch — that explains latency. we want filler wait under 20ms for these short requests.

sam: ran quick metric queries:
- avg_microbatch_size last 15m = 1.7 (normal ~6.1)
- queue_depth distribution = heavy tail (many tiny entries)
- max_batch_tokens currently set to 1024, max_batch_size=64, prefill_ms=100

kai: prefill_ms=100 is high for low-token QPS workloads. it delays coalescing. but here we still saw microbatches with wait_ms=12 and 118 — suggests heuristic aborts coalescing early because of fairness cutoff.

alex: suspect the fairness heuristic that prevents tenant padding to hit their share is too strict: it rejects waiting fillers if tenant_share < threshold, letting small batches dispatch. combination of smaller tokens and strict fairness -> tiny inefficient batches.

nico: I can reproduce locally with a simple loadgen: 200 clients, payload 10-15 tokens, scheduler v2.3.7 + fairness cutoff 0.05 -> average microbatch 1.9. Reverted to v2.3.6 -> average microbatch 6.3 and throughput back.

support: customer timeline aligns with our rollout window. they started seeing issues ~30m after the deploy.

maria: quick mitigation options:
1) temporarily relax fairness cutoff (set fairness_min_share=0.02 -> 0.01) so filler requests are allowed to pad batches.
2) lower prefill_ms to 20ms for pools serving short-token workloads.
3) pin PulseAI to a new dedicated pool without noisy neighbors and roll back scheduler to v2.3.6.

sam: also found autoscaler behavior odd: the pool didn't scale up because autoscaler uses CPU headroom metric not GPU runqueue. for this workload CPU low, so no extra capacity granted even though latency high.

kai: ok high-level action:
- rollback scheduler v2.3.7 from d-pulse-01 (safe immediate) -> reduces inefficient fairness enforcement.
- set prefill_ms=20 and fairness_min_share=0.01 on that pool as hotfix.
- create ticket to adjust autoscaler to consider gpu_queue_depth/gpu_util metric.

alex: I'll run commands to patch pool config now.

alex: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/pools/d-pulse-01/config -d '{"prefill_ms":20,"fairness_min_share":0.01}'`

infra-bot: [job] applying config change to d-pulse-01...

infra-bot: [job] config change applied.

sam: rolling scheduler rollback now.

infra-bot: [deploybot] rolling back scheduler on d-pulse-01 to v2.3.6...

infra-bot: [deploybot] rollback complete.

alex: post-fix quick readouts (5m after):
- avg_microbatch_size = 5.8 -> much closer to baseline
- gpu_util = 78% -> good
- p50 latency back to 48ms, p95 140ms -> improving

support: PulseAI confirms qps restored for their baseline test. They still saw a few 429s earlier due to a rate-limiter interaction; I cleared their transient burst credits.

maria: follow-ups:
- track longer-term regressions, keep an eye on other pools rolled to v2.3.7.
- create postmortem about fairness heuristic edge-case + add integration test to load tests (short-token high-concurrency).
- schedule autoscaler change to include gpu_queue_depth metric in next sprint.

kai: note: for customers with uniform short-token requests, we should ship a recommended pool config (prefill_ms=20, max_batch_tokens=512, fairness_min_share=0.01) in the console templates.

alex: thanks all. @oncall can you keep watch and close once stable? :thumbsup:

oncall: watching. will report by 09:30 UTC.

sam: adding a short diagnostic script to quickly extract microbatch stats per-tenant: `python tools/diagnostics/microbatch_stats.py --pool d-pulse-01 --window 10m` — drop into runbook.

support: closing loop with PulseAI, they asked for an RCA email. I'll draft and share.

nico: logging this thread into incidents/ and labelling "scheduler-fairness-regression".

alex: great job team.

oncall: 09:22 UTC update: metrics stable for 12m, no regressions seen. closing in 1h unless spike.
